gold: Type B lactic acidosis secondary to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
e7_s4_rationale: The presence of diffuse lymphadenopathy and a large mesenteric mass on CT abdomen, along with the patient's symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, are highly suggestive of lymphoma. The elevated lactate levels and acidotic pH also indicate possible bowel ischemia due to the mesenteric mass encasing the mesenteric vasculature, which can be a complication of lymphoma.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
e7_s4_rejected.why: While possible, the presence of diffuse lymphadenopathy is more typical of lymphoma than a gastrointestinal stromal tumor.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
e7_s4_rejected.why: Desmoid tumors are rare and typically do not present with such extensive lymphadenopathy or elevated lactate levels.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Sclerosing mesenteritis
e7_s4_rejected.why: Sclerosing mesenteritis usually presents with a more chronic course and does not typically cause the acute symptoms or the significant lactate elevation seen in this patient.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Carcinoid tumor
e7_s4_rejected.why: Carcinoid tumors can cause abdominal pain and bowel obstruction, but the presence of diffuse lymphadenopathy and the pattern of lactate elevation are not typical for this diagnosis.

B07_pred: Small intestine neuroendocrine tumor (SINET) with mesenteric desmoplasia; Mesenteric lymphoma
